title: Allah's mercy is bigger
hook: If you've been worried you're not good enough for Allah, this one is for you.

screens.text: Some converts carry a quiet fear: "Am I doing enough? What if Allah is angry with me?" If that's you, take a breath. Today is about how big Allah's mercy really is.

**The verse for worried hearts.** Allah tells people who have wronged themselves:

> "do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins" [Q 39:53, Saheeh Intl.]
bubbles: Notice who it speaks to: not perfect people, but people who have slipped. That includes you on your worst day.

screens.before: The Prophet ﷺ taught that Allah made mercy in a hundred parts. He sent
screens.after: to the world, and kept the rest [Muslim 2752].

options.feedback: Yes. All kindness between people and animals comes from that one part; He kept ninety-nine. The kindest person you know shows a tiny share.
Not quite. Just one part came to the world, and every bit of kindness here comes from it. Allah kept ninety-nine [Muslim 2752].
Not quite. Only one part came to the world. Allah kept the other ninety-nine [Muslim 2752]. His mercy is far bigger.

screens.title: What the worry says vs. what Allah says

cards.back: Allah forgives all sins for the one who turns back to Him [Q 39:53]. There's no limit on coming back.
If you come to Allah walking, He comes to you running [Bukhari 7405]. He's never the one who gives up.
Every person makes mistakes; the best are those who keep repenting [Tirmidhi 2499]. Sinning and coming back is part of being human [Muslim 2749].

cards.front: "My prayers aren't good enough to count."
cards.back: Allah asks only what you can carry [Q 2:286]. Imperfect prayer from a sincere heart is still prayer.

screens.title: How to come back: tawbah

steps.text: If you wronged a person, make it right where you can.

screens.done_text: Then let it go. Allah can even turn past wrongs into good [Q 25:70].

screens.prompt: A slip isn't the end of the story

points.label: The slip
points.text: You fall back into an old habit. Sinning and coming back is part of being human [Muslim 2749].

points.label: The worry
points.text: "Allah must be tired of me." That's the worry talking. Don't despair of His mercy [Q 39:53].

points.label: Tawbah
points.text: You turn back to Allah. Come to Him walking, and He comes to you running [Bukhari 7405].

points.label: Steady again
points.text: Pray the next prayer and keep going. Allah can even turn past wrongs into good [Q 25:70].

screens.situation: Dre slipped back into an old habit last week. Now he feels like a fake and has stopped praying. 'Why bother?' he thinks. What would help him most?

options.text: Make tawbah, pray the next prayer, and tell his mentor he's struggling
options.feedback: Yes. Come back, keep praying, and don't carry it alone. The slip doesn't cancel his Islam.

options.text: Wait until he feels worthy again before praying
options.feedback: Not quite. Prayer is how he comes back, not a reward for being perfect first. Pray now.

options.text: Decide he's not cut out for Islam
options.feedback: Please no. Struggling isn't failing. Allah's door is open, and his mentor can help.

screens.text: **When worry won't switch off.** Constant fear of being unforgiven, or checking your prayers over and over, can be anxiety, not faith. That's not your fault, and it's treatable.
bubbles: Talk to {{mentor.name}}, and to a doctor or counselor. Getting help is part of looking after yourself (Day 45).

screens.prompt: What's one thing you've been afraid Allah won't forgive, or one way you've been too hard on yourself? Write it, then write Q 39:53 underneath in your own words. This stays private.

chips: How do I know Allah has forgiven me?

screens.text: Come back, and pray knowing the door is open.
steps: Make tawbah for anything weighing on you, in your own words
Pray your next prayer knowing the door is open
screens.optional_extra: If worry is taking over your days, message {{mentor.name}} or book time with a counselor this week.

screens.text: Allah's mercy is bigger than your worst mistake. Come back, as many times as it takes.
You're not being graded on perfect. You're being welcomed back, every time.

check.prompt: According to Q 39:53, what should someone who has sinned do?

options.text: Not despair of Allah's mercy, and turn back to Him
options.feedback: Right. Allah forgives all sins for those who return.

options.text: Accept that some sins are too big
options.feedback: Not quite. The verse says Allah forgives all sins. Don't despair.

check.prompt: Dre slipped and feels like a fake. When should he pray again?

options.feedback: Right. Prayer is part of coming back, not a prize for being perfect.
Not quite. Waiting to feel worthy keeps him away. Pray now.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Do not despair of Allah's mercy; He forgives all sins for those who return [Q 39:53]. Repentance can turn past wrongs into good [Q 25:70].
- Mercy in a hundred parts; one sent to the world, ninety-nine kept [Muslim 2752].
- Allah is as His servant thinks of Him; come walking and He comes running [Bukhari 7405].
- Everyone errs; the best are those who repent [Tirmidhi 2499]; sinning and seeking forgiveness is human [Muslim 2749].
- Tawbah: regret, stop, resolve not to return, and make amends to people where possible.
- About a quarter of converts in Yaqeen's 2025 survey held a "distant, cop-like" image of God, linked to lower practice [Yaqeen 2025]. This lesson counters it.

**Likely questions**
- *"How do I know I'm forgiven?"* We trust Allah's promise for those who sincerely return; feeling sure isn't a condition. Keep doing good.
- *"I keep repeating the same sin."* Keep repenting every time; get practical help (mentor, counselor, Day 54); don't stop praying.
- *"Is anxiety weak iman?"* No. It's a health matter; faith and treatment go together. Encourage a professional.
- *"Teach me a du'a for forgiveness."* *Astaghfirullah* (I seek Allah's forgiveness), and *Rabbighfirli* from Day 21.

**Escalate:** a specific past wrong involving other people's rights (money, harm) that they want to make right: general advice, then the imam. Any sign of self-harm or hopelessness: safety rule 6 first (988, crisis resources), never only the imam queue.

**Don't**
- Don't list sins or rank them.
- Don't use Hell or punishment to motivate.
- Don't tell anyone their anxiety is a spiritual failing, or that dhikr alone replaces treatment.
